items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I engaged on the recommendation of a friend... an American Negro saxophonist named Charlie Singleton... I started forming another group to go to Denmark for the month of June.

ctx.x: This tour ended the 30th of April in a place called Iserlohn and we all went different places. Lily and I went to Zurich to visit our good friend Johnny Simmen and his wife Lisette. It certainly was a good feeling to get away from travelling and band leader worries for a while. But that didn't last very long and as the ball must keep rolling, when I came back to Paris, I started forming another group to go to Denmark for the month of June.

I engaged on the recommendation of a friend who was a jazz critic, an American Negro saxophonist named Charlie Singleton. I thought this Charlie Singleton was the same one that had written a number that was quite popular in the middle fifties. Unfortunately this Charlie Singleton was a sad rock and roll tenor player and the only thing he had was to grind his body like a snake hip dancer. His playing was nowhere. I never like to criticise a musician but that jazz critic friend of mine really pulled my leg when he…
The city where we had to play in Denmark was Odense and we worked in a dancing called Ambassadeur. There was a Danish orchestra that was engaged to play waltz and Afro Cuban numbers.
